name: elite2-firefox-win-usb-xinput
label: Xbox Elite Series 2 — USB / Firefox XInput

environment.mode: XInput with unknown onboard paddle assignments

sources.says: All three connections are supported on Windows 10/11.
Windows XInput backend handles any successful XInputGetState device.

environment.reason: Conditional on Windows routing this connection through XInput. No per-connection physical browser dump was found.

sources.says: The XInput poll emits events only for changed buttons/axes.
Construction, input events and SyncState update the DOM timestamp using performance.now.
GetGamepads returns existing objects without calling SyncState.
SetIsBackground invokes SyncGamepadState when returning to foreground and also some unchanged background-state calls.

timestampPolicy.reason: Change policy models ordinary foreground polling; construction starts at performance.now. Browser background/foreground synchronization and timer precision reduction are outside this synthetic fixture.

sources.says: ScanForXInputDevices passes literal xinput to AddGamepad, with no VID/PID.
XInput AddGamepad specifies Standard mapping.
XInput adds kStandardGamepadButtons and only standard masks, including Guide.
XInput exposes four normalized stick axes.
Centered sticks approximately report zero and can drift.

axesRest.reason: Ideal zero center, not a captured resting sample. Trigger release is button value 0 and no trigger axes are returned.

sources.says: Windows backend supplies zero haptics and leaves a haptics TODO.
Gamepad has hapticActuators but no vibrationActuator attribute.
Browser backend sends A to standard button 0.
Browser backend sends B to standard button 1.
Browser backend sends X to standard button 2.
Browser backend sends Y to standard button 3.
Browser backend sends Left bumper to standard button 4.
Browser backend sends Right bumper to standard button 5.
Trigger 6 copies XInput byte /255; pressed at byte >=30.
The pressed/value overload copies pressed into touched, including XInput triggers below the threshold.
Trigger 7 copies XInput byte /255; pressed at byte >=30.
The pressed/value overload copies pressed into touched, including XInput triggers below the threshold.
Browser backend sends View to standard button 8.
Browser backend sends Menu to standard button 9.
Browser backend sends Left stick click to standard button 10.
Browser backend sends Right stick click to standard button 11.
Browser backend sends D-pad up to standard button 12.
Browser backend sends D-pad down to standard button 13.
Browser backend sends D-pad left to standard button 14.
Browser backend sends D-pad right to standard button 15.
Browser backend sends Xbox to standard button 16.
Axes 0/1 are left X/Y; Y is inverted for down-positive.
Axes 2/3 are right X/Y; Y is inverted for down-positive.
XInput backend only maps the standard 17 buttons; it has no paddle mask.

P1.reason: No independent paddle index in this backend. An onboard assignment may repeat another control; this fixture does not guess those assignments.

sources.says: Backend maps standard controls, not an Elite profile selector.
Dedicated button switches default and three saved custom profiles.

Profile button.reason: Stored profiles are programmable and their contents are unknown. The selector has no distinct button index here.

sources.says: Elite Series 2 has three levels of trigger depth.
Controller automatically recognizes trigger-lock adjustments.
Browser exposes normalized trigger values, with no trigger-lock state field.

evidence.reason: This switch records physical travel only. set() supplies the browser's normalized value, so no guessed travel-to-value curve is applied.

sources.says: Elite Series 2 has three levels of trigger depth.
Controller automatically recognizes trigger-lock adjustments.
Browser exposes normalized trigger values, with no trigger-lock state field.

evidence.reason: This switch records physical travel only. set() supplies the browser's normalized value, so no guessed travel-to-value curve is applied.

sources.says: Dedicated button selects default or one of three programmable profiles.

Profile button.reason: The stored remapping slots and firmware are not known. No invented paddle aliases or profile-button signal is emitted.

notes: Exact browser backend layout, with connection routing inferred; no real-device Gamepad API dump was found.
Buttons 0–16 and axes 0–3 follow the standard layout. No hat axis; D-pad is buttons 12–15.
All released button values are 0, pressed/touched false. Trigger values are quantized byte/255.
P1–P4 cannot be bound as independent browser inputs here. Onboard remappings may repeat existing controls, but their stored assignments are deliberately unknown.
Profile button and trigger-lock switches have no independent Gamepad fields. Physical travel is recorded, not transformed with invented ratios.
vibrationActuator is absent; null in profile data means omit the property. Firefox hapticActuators is not implemented by this Windows backend.
Firefox trigger touched mirrors pressed: byte values 1 through 29 have value greater than zero, pressed false and touched false.

Timestamp starts at performance.now and changes with input during ordinary foreground polling. Firefox also updates on window synchronization; background/foreground scheduling and clock precision reduction are not reproduced.
